details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- README.md:338 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The manual-bootstrap instructions still say to create only three core wrappers, omitting the responder wrapper.
  WHY: Users following the instructions may leave standalone clarification questions without a listener.
- README.md:1145 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The Clarify documentation says credentials and other external inputs cause a `BLOCKED:` handoff, contradicting the updated placeholder behavior.
  WHY: Operators may expect credential-dependent issues to pause for human input, while the workflow continues with placeholders; severity disagreement exists, and the highest severity is reported.
- README.md:835 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The respond-wrapper example omits the job-level event predicate and `id-token: write` permission.
  WHY: Consumers following the example may create a wrapper without the trust gate, allowing it to run on untrusted comments.
- README.md:1191 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The documentation describes auto-answering clarification questions on orchestrator issues but omits standalone issues.
  WHY: Operators may be misled about the workflow's scope.
- README.md:(absent) | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The repository variables table does not document `STANDALONE_CLARIFY_RESPOND_ENABLED`.
  WHY: Operators cannot discover or configure the feature from the README.
- tests/test_update_workflows_guardrails.py:73-87 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `test_install_profile_docs_and_agents_contracts` lacks the manual-bootstrap assertions shown in the PR diff.
  WHY: The test cannot verify that the README names the fourth wrapper and documents the fallback.
- workflow-templates/profiles/core.txt:(end of file — 6 lines) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The core install profile still lists six wrappers and omits `ai-orchestrate-clarify-respond.yml`.
  WHY: Default core-profile installations do not receive the responder wrapper, leaving standalone questions unanswered.
- README.md:341-344 (approx, based on PR diff context) | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The README says credential-dependent issues cause Clarify to emit `BLOCKED: <reason>`.
  WHY: Operators following this guidance may expect the pipeline to pause for human input, but it continues using placeholders.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "The `core` install profile now includes the issue-comment responder wrapper, so its default delegation does not silently leave standalone questions unanswered."
  expected_change_site: workflow-templates/profiles/core.txt, agents.md PROFILE.name=core line, README.md install-profiles section
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  EVIDENCE: core.txt has only 6 lines (the old six-wrapper manifest); agents.md:776 lists the old 6-wrapper set; README.md:835 shows the old three-wrapper manual-bootstrap text; the CI check-run snapshot at head `1febf9f22c28af378ab2be89bf65d2663a285278` reports 0 failures but the checkout at those files has old content.
- requirement: "clarify.yml's 'Clarification required' Telegram alert is skipped when the questions were auto-answered or delegated" and "The worker sends the same CRITICAL alert itself if it fails and a question has no RECOMMENDED option to fall back to."
  expected_change_site: README.md Telegram notifications section (line 2489 area, "Phase-tracked alerts")
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  EVIDENCE: The README at line 2489 still describes old behavior: "Clarification required — sent by clarify.yml and plan.yml ... Orchestrator-managed issues skip this alert because clarify uses a label-based fast path." The PR DIFF shows this was updated with the delegation/worker language, but the checkout still shows old content.
- requirement: "The variable STANDALONE_CLARIFY_RESPOND_ENABLED is documented"
  expected_change_site: README.md repository variables table
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  EVIDENCE: `grep` finds no `STANDALONE_CLARIFY_RESPOND_ENABLED` in README.md. The row is absent.
- requirement: "prompts/mode-clarify.txt: no longer emits BLOCKED: for credentials, undecided branch names or future commits. BLOCKED: stays for auth-walled content the task depends on."
  expected_change_site: README.md near line 1145 (the "Open an issue" section describing Clarify behavior)
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: README.md line 1145 still states "If required input is external and non-synthesizable (for example branch/SHA/credential/external URL), it emits a `BLOCKED: <reason>` handoff"; README.md:1145 still says "If required input is external and non-synthesizable (for example branch/SHA/credential/external URL), it emits a `BLOCKED: <reason>` handoff" — listing "credential" as a BLOCKED trigger.
- requirement: The test should check that both README section headings exist before indexing the chained split results.
  expected_change_site: tests/test_update_workflows_guardrails.py, `test_install_profile_docs_and_agents_contracts`
  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: `readme.split("### 2. Create wrapper workflows", 1)[1].split("#### Optional wrappers", 1)[0]` indexes split results without verifying either heading is present.

=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- README.md:338 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Still reads "At minimum, create these three core wrappers." The LAST RUN DIFF and PR DIFF both show this was changed to name `ai-clarify.yml`, `ai-plan.yml`, `ai-implement.yml`, and `ai-orchestrate-clarify-respond.yml` with instructions for the fourth wrapper and the fallback.
  WHY: Manual-bootstrap users following the README will create only three wrappers, leaving standalone clarification questions with no listener. The default delegation suppresses the alert but nothing answers.
- README.md:1145 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: "If required input is external and non-synthesizable (for example branch/SHA/credential/external URL), it emits a `BLOCKED: <reason>` handoff" contradicts the PR's new clarify prompt behavior where credentials and setup are carried forward as UPPER_SNAKE_CASE placeholders and never block.
  WHY: Operators reading this section will expect credential-dependent issues to stop for human input; the updated workflow will answer them with placeholders and continue.
- README.md:835 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The respond wrapper example does not include the job-level event predicate or `id-token: write` permission. The PR DIFF shows these were added.
  WHY: A consumer following the README example creates a wrapper without the trust gate; the wrapper runs on every comment rather than only trusted `github-actions[bot]` or OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR comments.
- README.md:1191 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Still reads "Auto-answers clarification questions on orchestrator issues" instead of "orchestrator issues and standalone issues."
  WHY: Stale documentation misleads operators about the scope of the workflow.
- README.md:(absent) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The variable row `STANDALONE_CLARIFY_RESPOND_ENABLED` is missing from the repository variables table.
  WHY: Operators cannot discover or configure the feature from the README.
- tests/test_update_workflows_guardrails.py:73-87 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `test_install_profile_docs_and_agents_contracts` does not contain the `manual_bootstrap` split assertions that the LAST RUN DIFF shows were added.
  WHY: The test cannot verify that the README's manual-bootstrap section names the fourth wrapper and documents the fallback. The test silently accepts any content in that section.
- workflow-templates/profiles/core.txt:(end of file — 6 lines) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The core install profile is still a 6-wrapper manifest. The PR DIFF adds `ai-orchestrate-clarify-respond.yml` as the seventh wrapper. The checkout has the old 6-line file.
  WHY: Default core-profile installations never receive the respond wrapper. Standalone questions are delegated into silence.

  Expected change site: workflow-templates/profiles/core.txt, agents.md PROFILE.name=core line, README.md install-profiles section
  Evidence of absence: core.txt has only 6 lines (the old six-wrapper manifest); agents.md:776 lists the old 6-wrapper set; README.md:835 shows the old three-wrapper manual-bootstrap text. The CI check-run snapshot at head `1febf9f22c28af378ab2be89bf65d2663a285278` reports 0 failures but the checkout at those files has old content.
  SEVERITY: critical
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

  Expected change site: README.md Telegram notifications section (line 2489 area, "Phase-tracked alerts")
  Evidence of absence: The README at line 2489 still describes old behavior: "Clarification required — sent by clarify.yml and plan.yml ... Orchestrator-managed issues skip this alert because clarify uses a label-based fast path." The PR DIFF shows this was updated with the delegation/worker language, but the checkout still shows old content.
  SEVERITY: high

  Expected change site: README.md repository variables table
  Evidence of absence: `grep` finds no `STANDALONE_CLARIFY_RESPOND_ENABLED` in README.md. The row is absent.
  SEVERITY: high
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- README.md:341-344 (approx, based on PR diff context) | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The README retains a statement claiming credential-dependent issues cause Clarify to emit `BLOCKED: <reason>`.
  WHY: This contradicts the updated prompt behavior implemented in this PR, which now instructs the model to carry credentials forward as placeholders. Operators following the outdated README will expect the pipeline to pause for human input (emitting `BLOCKED`) when credentials are missing, whereas it will instead continue using placeholders.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
